entries.notes: Founded by Amos Hoff, Prof. of Physics — Phoenix College faculty since 1937.
Club-funded and ground 24" f7 telescope installed on the Phoenix College campus.
Telescope de-commissioned.
Incorporated as a 501(c)(3) non-profit. Newsletter: Sky-Lines.

New Cassegrain optics for the Amos Hoff 24" reflector, ground by optician Don Loomis, unveiled November 21. Members toured Lowell Observatory's Andrews Mesa site in October, viewing the 13" astrocamera used to discover Pluto.
Observatory proposed for Paradise Valley Park (near Paradise Valley Community College). Proposal denied; 24" mirror sold and installed in a private observatory near Alpine, AZ.

Bruce Lanard elected President, with Steve Coe — later a noted deep-sky observer and author — as Vice President. Dr. Arthur Hoag, Director of Lowell Observatory, spoke on current research programs including the Hubble constant.
New logo adopted.
Newsletter renamed PAStimes.
Meeting location changed.
Meeting location changed.
pasaz.org domain registered for email.
Website hosting at pasaz.org / geocities.com. Became a member of the Astronomical League.

PAS ran an Astronomy Day "Space Stations" event with NASA, the U.S. Geological Survey, Lowell Observatory, and the International Dark Sky Association, drawing hundreds of families for hands-on astronomy activities.
Mars made its closest approach to Earth in nearly 60,000 years; PAS set up 17+ telescopes for a packed public Mars-viewing event.
Meeting location changed.
PAS joined the Sally Ride Science Festival at ASU, offering solar viewing and handing out hundreds of donated Sky & Telescope magazines to encourage girls in science.
Meeting location changed.
pasaz.org website redesigned on Google Sites.
The Phoenix Astronomical Society / Sam Insana Memorial Scholarship established, honoring former PAS President Sam Insana.
